notes:
FAULT VERDICT: fixed, and measured rather than eyeballed. Each leaf's outer edge now changes direction three times between the band and the front point (outer-edge bend at 35% along, the tip, and the notch apex) versus the "single straight edge, no facets" the previous QC recorded. Numbers in lockedFeatures[0].

HOWEVER - the previous QC's critical finding was a false positive, and this matters for the pipeline. I measured candidate-1 with the same method: its tip-to-notch run is 24.69 deg (L, 160 columns, residual sd 0.32 px) and 23.19 deg (R), with apex vertices at (276, 525) and (609, 527). Candidate-1 already had the stepped outline, geometrically almost identical to candidate-2 (run angle moved only 24.7 -> 23.8 deg on the left). The "hexagonal outline entirely absent / plain triangular point collar" claim in qc.json is not supported by the image. One generation was spent correcting a fault that did not exist, and the correction text did not measurably change anything. Any further correction aimed at the step alone will likewise do nothing - the step is already right.

RECOMMENDATION: I score every category below the 98 bar, but I would NOT re-shoot on the strength of these findings alone. All three major findings share one root cause - the collar leaves sit ~9-10 deg steeper and the V ~30% shallower than a flat 2D technical drawing shows - which is drape/camera attitude, not option identity. A customer comparing this against any other shirt collar in the catalog would identify the faceted stepped leaf instantly. If the retry budget allows exactly one more attempt, spend it on the ratio-based attitude language in the corrections above and lock everything in lockedFeatures; if it does not, this is a waiver candidate (no critical findings, identity feature correct) rather than a discard.

MEASUREMENT PROVENANCE / WHAT I COULD NOT MEASURE:
1. No centimetre figure is recoverable. The tech pack carries no printed dimension callout (whole 226x226 drawing contains 1,188 dark pixels, all line-work, zero digits or text). Every number above is a ratio. S = tip-to-tip collar point span (drawing 158.5 px, render 767.0 px); leaf-length frame used as the independent cross-check.
2. Landmark validated first: I used two normalisations and report where they disagree. Band-corner span as unit makes the band height agree to 2% but the leaf length disagree by 17%; tip-span as unit makes the leaf front-edge length agree to 1.3% but the V depth disagree by 31%. The front-point depth error is the only one that survives BOTH (-31% / -18%), which is why it is the strongest dimensional finding.
3. Span checked on every fit. The tip-to-notch runs were fitted over 146/166 columns of the ~210 available, deliberately excluding ~30 px at each corner, and the apexes were then relocated by continuous tracking across the corner so no apex is an extrapolation. Both apexes and both tips are interior points of their search ranges, not saturating against a crop boundary.
4. Two measurements I discarded rather than reported: (a) an outer-edge straightness trace that jumped onto the shoulder seam at y~375 and returned a bogus 0.267 sagitta ratio - the collar edge and the shoulder seam cross there; (b) a line-intersection estimate of the drawing's V vertex that gave y=159 because both arms curve inward near the bottom. The true vertex is (108.75, 170) +/-2 by direct 16x pixel inspection, and the lowest red pixel at y=172 is the placket tail below the vertex, a different feature.
5. Could NOT measure: collar stand height at the front (hidden behind the leaves in the drawing, hidden by the viewing angle in the render); stitch gauge or stitches-per-inch (the drawing is single line-work at 226 px with no stitch callout, so the render's 0.022 S edge-stitch inset has nothing to compare against - it is neither confirmed nor contradicted); the drawing's inner neckband V (a second convergence at ~0.20 S below the tip line) - I can see the corresponding second line in the render but not confidently enough to give a number.

SPEC BUG worth fixing upstream: spec.json / prompt.json list "hexagon pocket" as a required shape token for a shirt collar. That is a text-extraction artefact - the drawing shows no pocket. The render correctly has none. If a future attempt renders a pocket to satisfy that token it would be a critical failure caused by the spec, not the model. Also note spec.json describes a "band-style stand collar" while the drawing plainly shows a turndown collar with two pointed leaves; the drawing wins, the render followed the drawing, and that is correct.
